source_title: DreamVideo-Omni: Omni-Motion Controlled Multi-Subject Video Customization with Latent Identity Reinforcement Learning

concepts.label: latent identity reward model
concepts.description: A specialized AI model that evaluates how well a generated video preserves a person's appearance (identity) while they are moving, and provides feedback scores directly in the compressed video representation — without needing to fully decode the video first.
concepts.why_innovative: By scoring identity quality inside the compressed (latent) space rather than the full pixel space, it dramatically cuts the computing cost of identity-aware training and enables richer feedback during video generation, something previous methods couldn't do efficiently.

concepts.label: latent identity reward feedback learning
concepts.description: A training strategy where the video-generation model learns to better preserve people's appearances by receiving quality scores (rewards) computed directly on compressed video data, guiding it to fix identity mistakes without expensive pixel-level processing.
concepts.why_innovative: This approach sidesteps the heavy computational burden of decoding full video frames just to measure identity quality, making reinforcement-learning-based identity preservation practical at scale for the first time.

concepts.label: group and role embeddings
concepts.description: Learnable tags added to motion signals (like bounding boxes or movement paths) that explicitly tell the AI which motion belongs to which specific person or object in a multi-person scene.
concepts.why_innovative: Without these tags, AI models confuse which movements go with which character in complex scenes; these embeddings eliminate that ambiguity, enabling reliable independent control of multiple subjects simultaneously.

concepts.label: condition-aware 3d rope
concepts.description: A modified positional encoding (a way of telling the AI where things are in space and time) that assigns unique spatial and temporal coordinates to each different type of input — such as appearance images, bounding boxes, and camera movements — so the model can handle all of them together without confusion.
concepts.why_innovative: Handling multiple heterogeneous control signals (appearance, motion, camera) simultaneously in one model is extremely difficult; this encoding makes joint training stable and fast, which is the key to building a truly unified video control framework.

concepts.label: hierarchical motion injection
concepts.description: A design where bounding-box (global position) information is fed into every layer of the video generation network, rather than just the first layer, so spatial guidance is reinforced throughout the entire process.
concepts.why_innovative: Injecting motion guidance at every level of the network ensures global positioning cues are never lost during generation, resulting in much more precise control over where objects appear and move in the video.

concepts.label: omni-motion control
concepts.description: A unified system that simultaneously controls three levels of movement in a generated video: overall object placement (global), fine-grained body part movements like limbs (local), and camera motion — all at once.
concepts.why_innovative: Prior methods could only handle one type of motion control at a time; combining all three in a single framework unlocks cinematic-level video generation that closely mirrors how real-world videos are filmed.

concepts.label: dreamomni bench
concepts.description: A new evaluation dataset of over 1,000 real-world videos with detailed annotations, specifically designed to test AI video models on both preserving multiple people's appearances and executing complex multi-level motion control at the same time.
concepts.why_innovative: Existing benchmarks tested identity preservation or motion control separately, never together; this benchmark fills that critical gap, enabling fair and comprehensive comparison of future video generation methods.
